controller_actions.task: Write module.py only. It must expose solve(data) implementing this contract exactly. Python standard library only; no I/O, no dynamic code execution, no external packages. Input: {"ops": list of operation objects}. Each operation has "kind" and, depending on kind, "amount" and/or "id". Apply operations in order and return {"balance": int, "held": int, "available": int}, where available = balance - held. Validation per operation, checked in this order: (1) kind must be one of credit, debit, hold, release, otherwise raise ValueError. (2) For credit, debit, hold: amount must be an integer >= 1; booleans are not integers and raise ValueError. (3) For hold: id must not already name an active hold; for release: id must name an active hold; violation raises ValueError. (4) For debit and hold: amount must not exceed currently available funds (balance - held), otherwise ValueError. Effects: credit increases balance; debit decreases balance; hold adds an active hold of amount under id (held increases, balance unchanged); release removes the hold named by id and ignores any amount field (held decreases). The first failing operation raises and no result is returned. Empty ops list returns zeros. Do not mutate the input. The previous candidate was wrong (it ignored holds and debits); do not reuse it.

Write test_cases.json only. It must be a JSON list of at least four distinct test cases, each with "input" and exactly one of "output" (expected JSON result) or "error" (exception class name, e.g. "ValueError"). Extra descriptive fields such as "name" are allowed. Derive every expectation strictly from this contract, not from any existing implementation.

Contract: Implement solve(data) for {"ops": list of operations}. Each operation is an object with "kind" and, depending on kind, "amount" and/or "id". Apply operations in order and return {"balance": int, "held": int, "available": int}, where available = balance - held. Per operation, checked in exactly this order: (1) kind must be one of credit, debit, hold, release; otherwise ValueError. (2) For credit, debit, hold, amount must be an integer >= 1; otherwise ValueError. Booleans are not integers and raise ValueError. (3) For hold, id must not already name an active hold; for release, id must name an active hold; violation raises ValueError. (4) For debit and hold, amount must not exceed currently available funds (balance - held); otherwise ValueError. Effects: credit increases balance; debit decreases balance; hold adds an active hold of amount under id (held increases, balance unchanged); release removes the hold named by id and ignores any amount field. The first failing operation raises and no result is returned. Empty ops list returns zeros.

Include cases covering: empty ops; credit then debit; hold reducing available with balance unchanged; release restoring available; release ignoring an amount field; debit or hold exceeding available funds (ValueError); duplicate hold id (ValueError); release of unknown id (ValueError); invalid kind (ValueError); boolean amount (ValueError); zero or negative amount (ValueError). Use only standard JSON. Each case must be distinct.
